title: The two regular-denominator tensor maps have the same kernel
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $F$ a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] with nonzero stalk at every point [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Suppose that on every affine open $U$, every associated prime of $\Gamma(U,F)$ is minimal among its associated primes (associated primes are prime annihilators of nonzero elements). Let $L$ be invertible [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s:\mathcal O_X\to K_X(L)$ a regular meromorphic section: its canonical extension $K_X\to K_X(L)$ is monomorphic [def-sc-meromorphic-module]. Put $I=\mathcal O_X\times_{K_X(L)}L$, with projections $i:I\to\mathcal O_X$ and $j:I\to L$. Using the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], write $f=(i\otimes F);\lambda_F:I\otimes F\to F$ and $g=(j\otimes F);\beta_{L,F}:I\otimes F\to F\otimes L$. Then $\ker(f)\hookrightarrow I\otimes F\xrightarrow{g}F\otimes L$ and $\ker(g)\hookrightarrow I\otimes F\xrightarrow{f}F$ are both zero.

source.place: Tag 02P2, lemma-make-maps-regular-section, affine injectivity calculation before the cokernel-support calculation

proof.text: By [lem-sc-hilbert-denominator-ideal-nowhere-dense], choose affine trivializing neighbourhoods with s=a/b and a,b ring nonzerodivisors. The coherent affine section theorem makes M=Gamma(U,F) finite. The affine stalk/support comparison and full stalk support give Supp(M)=Spec(A). Minimal primes over Ann(M) are associated primes; full support identifies these with ring minimal primes. Since every associated prime is minimal among associated primes, Ass(M) is contained in the ring minimal primes.

Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-affine-denominator-module] on the chart. Its map sigma:IM to M satisfies b sigma(z)=a z and is injective. The same lemma gives injectivity of M to M_b. Thus multiplication by a/b on IM has kernel zero.

The two pullback projections satisfy i;s=j;toMeromorphic. On a trivializing chart the map L to K_X(L) is injective: each allowed denominator acts injectively on L, detected on its stalks, and sheafification preserves a monomorphism. Clearing b in the fraction formula therefore identifies j(t) with (a/b)i(t). Apply the affine tensor-section comparison. On elementary tensors, f sends t tensor m to i(t)m and g sends it to j(t) tensor m. Consequently g equals multiplication by a/b after f, with the image of f equal to IM. Bilinearity extends the equality to all section tensors.

On every such affine chart, ker(f) maps to zero under g by this factorization. Conversely ker(g) maps to zero under f because multiplication by a/b on IM is injective. Restrict further to affine basic opens when testing a section of either kernel. These opens cover X; separatedness of the target sheaves glues the zero composites. This gives precisely kernel.ι(f);g=0 and kernel.ι(g);f=0, also on the empty scheme.

theorem hilbert_denominator_kernel_comparison {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F : X.Modules)
    (hFcoh : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F)
    (hFsupport : ∀ x : X, ¬ Subsingleton ((presheaf F).stalk x))
    (hFnoEmbedded : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U)
      (p : Ideal (Γ(X, U))),
      p ∈ associatedPrimes (Γ(X, U)) (Γ(F, U)) →
        Minimal (fun q : Ideal (Γ(X, U)) =>
          q ∈ associatedPrimes (Γ(X, U)) (Γ(F, U))) p)
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (s : unit X ⟶ meromorphicModule X L)
    (hs : Mono (meromorphicSectionMap X L s)) :
    kernel.ι ((pullback.fst s (toMeromorphicModule X L)) ▷ F ≫ (λ_ F).hom) ≫
        ((pullback.snd s (toMeromorphicModule X L)) ▷ F ≫ (β_ L F).hom) = 0 ∧
      kernel.ι ((pullback.snd s (toMeromorphicModule X L)) ▷ F ≫ (β_ L F).hom) ≫
        ((pullback.fst s (toMeromorphicModule X L)) ▷ F ≫ (λ_ F).hom) = 0
